title: Trump Fires NLRB Member Gwynne Wilcox and General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo
description_short: Trump Fires NLRB Member Gwynne Wilcox and General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo
description_medium: Trump fired NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox and General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo in late January 2025. Because the five-member board already had two vacancies, Wilcox's removal deprived it of a quorum and temporarily prevented it from issuing decisions. The stored claim that Trump fired all board members on January 20 is false.
description_long:
Trump removed National Labor Relations Board member Gwynne Wilcox and General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo in late January 2025. Reuters reported the dismissals on January 28. The immediate board-level consequence arose from Wilcox's departure: with two seats already vacant, the five-member body no longer had enough members for a quorum.

Without that quorum, the Board temporarily could not issue decisions. Abruzzo's dismissal concerned a separate leadership position and should not be counted as another removal from the five-member Board. Keeping the roles distinct explains why the membership change affected decision-making capacity.

The event was a substantial intervention in the agency's leadership, but the supplied reporting does not support saying Trump fired all sitting board members. Nor does it support dating all the dismissals to January 20. The absence of a Board quorum also should not be confused with the disappearance of every agency function. The documented account concerns named removals and the resulting constraint on Board decisions, leaving later staffing and litigation developments outside this event.

title: Brookings finds record 34% first-year turnover among Trump's senior White House team
description_short: Brookings finds record 34% first-year turnover among Trump's senior White House team
description_medium: Brookings calculated that 34% of Trump's senior White House 'A-Team' positions had turned over by his first anniversary, a modern record for first-year turnover and roughly double Ronald Reagan's 17% rate. Across Trump's full first term, Brookings counted four chiefs of staff. The stored 65% first-year figure and six-chief count are incorrect.
description_long:
Brookings' analysis found that 34% of Trump's senior White House 'A-Team' positions had turned over by his first anniversary. The study described that as a modern record for first-year turnover and compared it with Ronald Reagan's 17% rate. The comparison points to instability within the particular set of senior positions Brookings tracked.

The scope of the measure matters. An 'A-Team' turnover percentage is not a count of every employee in the White House or across the federal government. It also should not be replaced by the unsupported 65% first-year figure in the earlier account.

A separate Brookings retrospective counted four chiefs of staff over Trump's full first term, rather than six. These are different measurements covering different time spans: first-year turnover in senior positions and a full-term count of chiefs of staff. Together they support an account of unusually frequent leadership changes while keeping the underlying figures, comparison and periods distinct.
